bugs.title: Cancellation can leave descendant processes running
bugs.detail: terminate() sends SIGTERM to the process group but escalates to SIGKILL only if the direct Codex process remains alive. If Codex exits promptly while a descendant ignores SIGTERM, process.wait() succeeds and cleanup returns with the descendant still running. Cancellation, timeout, and server shutdown can therefore report termination while spawned commands continue executing and changing the workspace.
bugs.evidence: Reproduced using a session-leading parent with a child that ignores SIGTERM: after Workbench.terminate(parent), parent.returncode was -15 and os.kill(child_pid, 0) succeeded. The synthetic processes were subsequently killed.
bugs.fix: Check and terminate remaining process-group members independently of the direct parent's exit, and add a descendant-process cancellation test.
